text: Endpoint authentication tests must remain architecturally separate from ToolGateway governance tests because they verify different layers of the system. Endpoint tests confirm that HTTP routes reject unauthenticated requests with 403 Forbidden, while ToolGateway tests confirm that write tools are blocked in read_only mode and require valid approval tokens in build mode. Mixing these assertions leads to fragile tests that break when either layer changes independently. The auth front proved separation by running fourteen endpoint tests against FastAPI routes and separate ToolGateway tests for promotion_candidate_promote behavior. This separation improves maintainability and makes it explicit which layer failed when a regression occurs. Each test suite should assert its own boundary without implicitly depending on the other layer's state.
summary: Endpoint auth tests must stay separate from ToolGateway governance tests

text: Critical chat and run endpoints must not rely on localhost bypass for authentication. The security auth front hardened seven endpoints including POST /v2/chat/agent and POST /v2/agent/runs by applying require_strict_operator_access, which enforces BRAIN_ADMIN_TOKEN validation regardless of request origin. Unauthenticated requests receive 403 Forbidden even when originating from 127.0.0.1. This prevents accidental exposure when services run behind reverse proxies or when local tunnels are opened during debugging. The hardened endpoints also cover plan, execute, pause, resume, and cancel operations. Read_only mode gates remain active after authentication, ensuring write tools stay blocked. Tests confirmed that valid tokens return 200 OK while missing or invalid tokens consistently return 403.
summary: Critical chat/run endpoints must not rely on localhost bypass

text: Git should track code and reports, while runtime semantic memory must remain local and untracked. The memory git hygiene front demonstrated this by untracking semantic_memory.jsonl, FAISS indexes, promotion_audit.jsonl, and rollback_snapshots without deleting local files. Repository size stays manageable when mutable runtime state is excluded from version control. The .gitignore was updated to block memory semantic files, autonomous journal entries, and audit CSVs. A guard script inspects staged files and fails if any sensitive runtime path is added, modified, or copied. This boundary prevents accidental commits that would bloat the repository and expose mutable state. All 1756 JSONL records and 1747 FAISS vectors were preserved locally after untracking, proving safety.
summary: Git tracks code and reports; runtime memory remains local and ignored

text: The git staging guard must block memory files and secrets from being committed while allowing intentional untracking operations. The guard script at scripts/git_hygiene/check_no_sensitive_paths_staged.py inspects staged files and fails if any path under memory/semantic/, memory/rollback_snapshots/, or memory/autonomous_journal.jsonl appears as added, modified, or copied. It explicitly allows staged deletions because untracking requires removing files from the index without deleting local content. This distinction is critical: blocking deletions would prevent the hygiene workflow from completing. The guard also rejects environment files, secrets CSVs, and crdownload artifacts. Safe report artifacts under tmp_agent/front_* are permitted. The guard runs before every commit to ensure runtime memory never enters version control accidentally.
summary: Staging guard blocks memory/secrets while allowing deletion-based untracking

text: Promotion manifests must deduplicate by normalized text content rather than relying solely on unique candidate identifiers. The 08F front revealed that thirty-six submitted entries reduced to twenty-eight unique IDs and further to twenty-four unique normalized texts after deduplication. Candidate IDs can be distinct while representing semantically identical lessons, especially when candidates are generated from similar sources or when IDs are regenerated during pipeline transitions. Normalizing whitespace and case before comparing text bodies ensures truly unique content is promoted while duplicates are silently skipped. This practice prevents redundant canonical memory entries that degrade retrieval quality and inflate vector index size. The deduplication pipeline should be applied before any batch promotion to maintain semantic integrity and avoid teaching the same lesson multiple times with different identifiers.
summary: Promotion manifests must deduplicate by normalized text, not only by ID

text: Every batch promotion must create a rollback snapshot before the first write to canonical memory. The snapshot should include semantic_memory.jsonl, the FAISS index file, FAISS ids JSON, and promotion_audit.jsonl if it exists. If any candidate promotion fails during the batch, the system can restore the exact pre-promotion state by copying snapshot files back to the canonical directory. This safety mechanism was proven in the 08F front where twenty-four candidates were promoted in sequence with per-candidate verification. Without pre-write snapshots, a failed batch would leave the memory system in a partially promoted, inconsistent state that is difficult to diagnose and repair. Snapshots should be timestamped and stored under memory/rollback_snapshots/ with a SNAPSHOT_REASON.txt explaining the batch context and expected increment count.
summary: Every batch promotion must snapshot before the first write

text: Semantic retrieval verification should query by candidate text or meaningful phrase rather than by candidate identifier. Querying by candidate_id tests only structural presence in the index, not semantic embedding quality. The 09A front proved retrieval by searching phrases extracted from each promoted candidate's text body. For example, querying strict token authentication on critical agent endpoints returned the auth hardening candidate as the top result with a score of 0.8098. This confirms the embedding model correctly captured the semantic meaning of the lesson. Querying by ID would merely verify that an ID exists in the FAISS mapping, which is already checked during post-promotion validation. Retrieval E2E must exercise the actual search path that agents and operators will use in production.
summary: Retrieval verification should query by text phrase, not candidate_id

text: Agent-use probes after ingestion must use strict token authentication and read_only mode to prevent accidental mutations during verification. The 09A front probed Agent V2 by posting to /v2/chat/agent with X-Brain-Token set to a valid test token and mode explicitly set to read_only. Each probe returned HTTP 200 with a coherent answer reflecting the newly promoted lessons, confirming that the ingestion circuit is complete from promotion through retrieval to agent response. Using read_only mode ensures that even if the agent attempts to invoke a write tool, the ToolGateway will block it. This is a critical safety boundary: verification should never mutate canonical memory, trigger promotions, or execute trading operations. Auth headers must be present on every probe to confirm that the hardened endpoint behavior survives real traffic.
summary: Agent probes must use strict token auth and read_only mode

text: Local dry-run validation must verify candidate schema, safety flags, duplicate text, known domain, and confirm no writes occur before actual promotion. The 08C front established a validation pipeline that loads candidates from promotion_queue or semantic_staging, normalizes metadata, and checks for blank text, exposed secrets, raw chain-of-thought, and unknown domains. It also computes normalized text hashes and compares them against canonical memory to prevent duplicate ingestion. Crucially, the dry-run path must never write to semantic_memory.jsonl or FAISS. Any write during validation indicates a pipeline bug that could corrupt canonical memory. The validation summary should report total candidates, valid candidates, promotable candidates, and explicitly assert no_writes_performed. Only after this gate passes should the operator approve promotion with an explicit token.
summary: Dry-run validation must check schema, safety, duplicates, and zero writes

text: Successful promotion mutates local runtime memory, but those mutated files must never be staged or committed to Git. The canonical semantic memory and FAISS indexes represent mutable runtime state that changes with every promotion, rollback, or compaction. Committing these files would create noisy diffs, inflate repository size, and risk exposing transient state. The git hygiene front explicitly untracked all runtime memory files and added them to .gitignore. After every promotion, operators must verify that git status shows memory files as either ignored or untracked, never staged. The guard script provides an automated check, but human vigilance remains necessary because Git commands like git add -A could bypass targeted staging. The rule is absolute: memory mutation is a runtime operation, not a version control operation.
summary: Promoted memory must stay local and must not be staged or committed

text: Promotion tools can only load candidates from supported sources such as promotion_queue directories and semantic_staging JSONL files. Front-local artifacts like curated_candidates_09a.json are not natively supported by the standard PromotionPipelineAdapter loader. The 09A front worked around this by writing individual candidate JSON files into a temporary queue_dir and passing that path explicitly to promote_candidate. This narrow validated path avoids modifying the permanent promotion_queue or semantic_staging directories. Attempting to load unsupported paths directly would raise candidate_not_found errors because the adapter only scans known directories. When introducing new candidate sources, the correct approach is either to extend the adapter with a narrow loader or to write candidates into a temporary validated queue directory that the existing loader can consume. This preserves the boundary between front artifacts and canonical pipeline state.
summary: Promotion tools load from supported sources; front artifacts need narrow loader or temp queue

text: Ingestion scaling must proceed gradually from individual records to small batches before attempting any mass ingestion. The 09A front proved the end-to-end circuit with exactly three curated candidates, demonstrating that promotion, retrieval, and agent-use verification work correctly at small scale. Moving directly from zero to large batch sizes risks overwhelming validation pipelines, exhausting rollback storage, and making failure diagnosis difficult. The recommended progression is: first validate single-record promotion, then three-record controlled E2E, then twelve-record small batch, then medium batch sizes with enhanced deduplication and compaction. Each stage must pass retrieval E2E and agent-use probes before the next stage is authorized. This incremental approach also helps refine candidate quality thresholds, embedding model behavior, and retrieval scoring thresholds under realistic but limited load. Mass ingestion should only be attempted after small and medium batch stages are proven stable.
summary: Scale ingestion gradually from single records to small batches before mass ingestion
